arxiv-2102-08562.title: Mode-Assisted Joint Training of Deep Boltzmann Machines
arxiv-2102-08562.creator: Haik Manukian, Massimiliano Di Ventra
arxiv-2102-08562.description: Abstract The deep extension of the restricted Boltzmann machine (RBM), known as the deep Boltzmann machine (DBM), is an expressive family of machine learning models which can serve as compact representations of complex probability distributions. However, jointly training DBMs in the unsupervised setting has proven to be a formidable task.

arxiv-2202-04226.title: First-principles calculations for transient absorption of laser-excited magnetic materials
arxiv-2202-04226.creator: Shunsuke A. Sato
arxiv-2202-04226.description: Abstract We investigate the modification in the optical properties of laser-excited bulk cobalt and nickel using the time-dependent density functional theory at a finite electron temperature. As a result of the first-principles simulation, a complex change in the photoabsorption of the magnetic materials is observed around the M 2 , 3 M_{2,3} absorption edge.

arxiv-2301-04013.title: There is No Big Brother or Small Brother: Knowledge Infusion in Language Models for Link Prediction and Question Answering
arxiv-2301-04013.creator: Ankush Agarwal, Sakharam Gawade, Sachin Channabasavarajendra, Pushpak Bhattacharyya
arxiv-2301-04013.description: Abstract The integration of knowledge graphs with deep learning is thriving in improving the performance of various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. In this paper, we focus on knowledge-infused link prediction and question answering using language models, T5, and BLOOM across three domains: Aviation, Movie, and Web.

arxiv-2307-09553.title: Stream Types Conference: ; ;
arxiv-2307-09553.creator: Joseph W. Cutler, Christopher Watson, Emeka Nkurumeh, Phillip Hilliard, Harrison Goldstein, Caleb Stanford, Benjamin C. Pierce
arxiv-2307-09553.description: Abstract . We propose a rich foundational theory of typed data streams and stream transformers, motivated by two high-level goals: (1) The type of a stream should be able to express complex sequential patterns of events over time. And (2) it should describe the internal parallel structure of the stream to support deterministic stream processing on parallel and distributed systems.

arxiv-2311-13573.title: h h -vectors of edge rings of odd-cycle compositions
arxiv-2311-13573.creator: Kieran Bhaskara, Akihiro Higashitani, Nayana Shibu Deepthi
arxiv-2311-13573.description: Abstract . Let 𝕂 ⁡ [ G ] \mathbb{K}[G] be the edge ring of a finite simple graph G G . Investigating properties of the h h -vector of 𝕂 ⁡ [ G ] \mathbb{K}[G] is of great interest in combinatorial commutative algebra. However, there are few families of graphs for which the h h -vector has been explicitly determined.

arxiv-2402-18562.title: Dark Scattering: accelerated constraints from KiDS-1000 with ReACT and CosmoPower 2024 Dark Scattering: accelerated constraints from KiDS-1000 with ReACT and CosmoPower – 8
arxiv-2402-18562.creator: Karim Carrion, Pedro Carrilho, Alessio Spurio Mancini, Alkistis Pourtsidou, Juan Carlos Hidalgo
arxiv-2402-18562.description: Abstract We present constraints on the Dark Scattering model through cosmic shear measurements from the Kilo Degree Survey (KiDS-1000), using an accelerated pipeline with novel emulators produced with CosmoPower . Our main emulator, for the Dark Scattering non-linear matter power spectrum, is trained on predictions from the halo model reaction framework, previously validated against simulations.

arxiv-2406-12902.title: JavaBench: A Benchmark of Object-Oriented Code Generation for Evaluating Large Language Models Thanks: * Co-first authors.
arxiv-2406-12902.creator: Jialun Cao, Zhiyong Chen, Jiarong Wu, Shing-Chi Cheung, Chang Xu
arxiv-2406-12902.description: Abstract . Code generation benchmarks such as HumanEval are widely adopted to evaluate LLMs’ capabilities. However, after consolidating the latest 24 benchmarks, we noticed three significant imbalances. First, imbalanced programming language . 95.8% of benchmarks involve Python, while only 5 benchmarks involve Java, resulting in an insufficient understanding of LLMs’ capability to generate Java code. Second, imbalanced code granularity .

arxiv-2507-19411.title: SILS: Strategic Influence on Liquidity Stability and Whale Detection in Concentrated-Liquidity DEXs
arxiv-2507-19411.creator: Ali RajabiNekoo, Laleh Rasoul, Amirfarhad Farhadi, Azadeh Zamanifar
arxiv-2507-19411.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ali RajabiNekoo, Laleh Rasoul, Amirfarhad Farhadi, Azadeh Zamanifar. Traditional methods for identifying impactful liquidity providers (LPs) in Concentrated Liquidity Market Makers (CLMMs) rely on broad measures, such as nominal capital size or surface-level activity, which often lead to inaccurate risk analysis. The SILS framework offers a significantly more detailed approach, characterizing LPs not just as capital holders but as dynamic systemic agents whose actions directly impact market stability. This represents a fundamental paradigm shift from the static, volume-based analysis to a dynamic, impact-focused understanding.

arxiv-2507-22578.title: Nonlocal conservation laws for the two-dimensional Euler equation in vorticity form
arxiv-2507-22578.creator: Oleg I. Morozov
arxiv-2507-22578.description: Abstract We combine the construction of the canonical conservation law and the nonlocal cosymmetry to derive a collection of nonlocal conservation laws for the two-dimensional Euler equation in vorticity form. For computational convenience and simplicity of presentation of the results we perform a complex rotation of the independent variables.

arxiv-2509-19862.title: Parameter Estimation for Jump-Diffusion Stochastic Master Equations
arxiv-2509-19862.creator: Weichao Liang, Shuixin Xiao, Daoyi Dong, Ian R. Petersen
arxiv-2509-19862.description: Abstract This paper investigates parameter estimation for open quantum systems under continuous observation, whose conditional dynamics are governed by jump–diffusion stochastic master equations (SMEs) associated with quantum nondemolition (QND) measurements. Estimation of model parameters such as coupling strengths or measurement efficiencies is essential, yet in practice these parameters are often uncertain.

arxiv-2512-07090.title: Leveraging KV Similarity for Online Structured Pruning in LLMs
arxiv-2512-07090.creator: Jungmin Lee, Gwangeun Byeon, Yulhwa Kim, Seokin Hong
arxiv-2512-07090.description: Abstract Pruning has emerged as a promising direction for accelerating large language model (LLM) inference, yet existing approaches often suffer from instability because they rely on offline calibration data that may not generalize across inputs. In this work, we introduce Token Filtering , a lightweight online structured pruning technique that makes pruning decisions directly during inference without any calibration data.

pmc-10671211.title: Mesenchymal Stem Cells in the Pathogenesis and Therapy of Autoimmune and Autoinflammatory Diseases
pmc-10671211.creator: Lina N. Zaripova, Angela Midgley, Stephen E. Christmas, Michael W. Beresford, Clare Pain, Eileen M. Baildam, Rachel A. Oldershaw
pmc-10671211.description: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) modulate immune responses and maintain self-tolerance. Their trophic activities and regenerative properties make them potential immunosuppressants for treating autoimmune and autoinflammatory diseases. MSCs are drawn to sites of injury and inflammation where they can both reduce inflammation and contribute to tissue regeneration.

pmc-11557761.title: Prehabilitation Interventions for Cardiac Surgery to Prevent Postoperative Pulmonary Complications: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-11557761.creator: Junhua Wang, Hui Li, Wenjuan Yan, Na Xue, Jin Yin, Nawsherwan, Sha Yin
pmc-11557761.description: Background:Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) are associated with a higher risk of morbidity and mortality in patients undergoing cardiac surgery. We aimed to investigate the effect of preoperative interventions on PPCs and length of intensive care unit and hospital stay in patients undergoing cardiac surgery.

pmc-11799233.title: Leveraging AI-driven nudge theory to enhance hand hygiene compliance: paving the path for future infection control
pmc-11799233.creator: Samiksha Bhattacharjee, Sudip Bhattacharya
pmc-11799233.description: Hand hygiene is critical for preventing infections, yet maintaining compliance remains challenging across healthcare, schools, and communities. Despite strong evidence, lapses occur due to cognitive barriers, understaffing, limited resources, and antimicrobial resistance. Behavioral science highlights factors like time constraints and cognitive biases affecting adherence, with compliance rates as low as 40%.

pmc-13157712.title: Barriers, Perceptions, and Predictors for Utilizing Health-Related Technology Among Individuals Receiving Radiation Oncology Care
pmc-13157712.creator: Maria Serafini, Cory Heal, Hayden A Ansinelli, Christopher M Morrison, Quoc Anh Ho, Victor Gonzalez, Sun Yi, Charles C Hsu, Jared R Robbins
pmc-13157712.description: Introduction: For many people, mobile applications are pivotal to their daily lives. With a constantly increasing number of applications, the utilization of mobile health (mHealth) has augmented various aspects of clinical care outside of traditional clinical appointments, such as patient communication and monitoring. Despite these advancements, widespread adoption of these applications by cancer patients remains limited.

pmc-13355433.title: Rapid inactivation kinetics of a broad range of viruses on a continuously self-cleaning polymer surface
pmc-13355433.creator: Kacie M. Wells, Daniela Silva-Ayala, Sarah J. Dejarnette, Jeremy P. Faircloth, Padraic O'Reilly, Reza A. Ghiladi, Lee-Ann Jaykus, Frank Scholle, Anthony Griffiths, Richard J. Spontak
pmc-13355433.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Infections arising from a broadening variety of viruses are becoming increasingly widespread due to greater zoonotic transmission, with the COVID-19 pandemic exemplifying a global event that claimed the lives of millions worldwide. While targeted vaccines are being developed to thwart the spread of viral infections, they often become available to the public in response to an (expected) outbreak and must be repeatedly adjusted to account for mutations.

pmc-13457751.title: Subgroup variations in effectiveness of femoropopliteal sirolimus versus paclitaxel-coated balloon angioplasty: post hoc results of the randomised SIRONA trial
pmc-13457751.creator: Ulf Teichgräber, Maja Ingwersen, Thomas Lehmann, Stephanie Platzer, Ina Kunstmann, Sabine Steiner, Andrej Schmidt, Tim Wittig, Thomas Zeller, Marcus Thieme, Hans Krankenberg, Martin Werner, Marianne Brodmann, Nasser Malyar, Stefan Müller-Hülsbeck, Luca de Paoli, Oliver Schlager, Martin Austermann, G
pmc-13457751.description: IntroductionThe randomised SIRONA trial showed that sirolimus-coated balloon (SCB) angioplasty was non-inferior to paclitaxel-coated balloon angioplasty (PCB) regarding femoropopliteal primary patency. There was no difference in clinically driven target lesion revascularisation (cdTLR) rates between the treatment groups. This post-hoc analysis aimed to assess whether the overall results were consistent across different subgroups and selected post-baseline factors.

pmc-13490729.title: From difficulty score to clinical outcome: Evaluating IWATE-criteria correlation with postoperative complications and revision surgery in anatomical liver resection
pmc-13490729.creator: Saeed Aldarwish, Clemens Schafmayer, Sebastian Hinz
pmc-13490729.description: Backgrounds/AimsMinimally invasive hepatobiliary surgery has advanced considerably, with laparoscopic liver resection now widely adopted. The IWATE difficulty score is commonly used to classify the technical complexity of laparoscopic resections; however, its ability to predict postoperative morbidity across different surgical approaches remains uncertain.
